changes.description: Dark mode. Follows your system appearance by default; use the switch in the header to override it.
Release notes now mark each change with an icon and a key, so descriptions line up in a single column.
Build version and data date moved from the header into this dialog.
PAN-OS 12.1 and 12.2 are discovered and crawled again. Palo Alto moved their release notes onto the NGFW documentation book and every 12.x version had been missing from the database.
Release notes no longer lose older entries each time the site is rebuilt.
`bugdb build` writes release notes next to the bug database file instead of a fixed assets/ directory.
The nightly upstream check now verifies that each PAN-OS version is actually ingested, not just that its page loads.
Data baseline refreshed against the sitemap-driven crawler: roughly 1,600 additional versions discovered and bug ids keyed to more precise versions.
PAN-OS 10.0 removed — Palo Alto delisted its release notes upstream.
Much faster data collection: sitemap-driven discovery and a direct HTTP transport replace the browser crawl.
Incremental refreshes skip pages that have not changed upstream.
Cortex XDR data now comes from the documentation API.
Fixed PAN-OS 12.1 release detection and parsing
Content Security Policy and cross-site scripting hardening for the site.
Live progress reporting and a streaming fetch log.
Automated data-fidelity checks so a refresh can never silently lose bug data.
